_comment: REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. A registered type binds on EVERY action unless an entry says otherwise, and saying otherwise costs a stated `reason`. The minimal entry {"family": "..."} is the STRICT one -- adding a type is one line and it binds immediately. Inclusion is free; exclusion is the thing that takes effort.
_why: The first draft listed required steps explicitly per action, so adding a checker meant writing it AND remembering to add it to the list. Forget the second half and the checker runs, passes, and counts for nothing -- absence rendering as success, in the very file that defines what complete means. A registry you must remember to extend is a registry that will be incomplete.
_reasonless_narrowing: An `actions` or `when` narrowing with NO `reason` is IGNORED and the type falls back to required-for-all. This is the encoding_whitelist.txt convention, reused deliberately because it is already familiar here: nothing is suppressed until a human has actually looked. A typo in an exemption fails safe.
_unregistered: V8 rejects a record whose step is not listed here, record.py returns None, and the checker exits 2 -- so the pipeline blocks the moment someone wires in an unregistered check, loudly, at the desk of the person who can fix it. That is the pair that closes the hole: you cannot add a check that silently does not count, and you cannot register one that silently is not required.

build.reason: stub-first commits sorry-stubbed files on purpose, and CI at the PR owns build state; only a release asserts the corpus builds

check_encoding.reason: its property is tracked TEXT files; a BOM test on a font or a published PDF is meaningless. Stated as an exclusion rather than an extension allow-list on purpose: a new text extension must NOT silently fall out of scope, which is the direction an allow-list fails in

check_frozen.reason: superseded by the independent-git-spaces rewrite; the frozen baselines describe a topology that no longer exists, so the freeze comparison cannot succeed and never will. STILL REGISTERED on purpose -- Tim, 2026-08-23: 'I have no problem if you want to still allow it to be submitted, it just shouldn't be required in order to pass.' Recording stays valid; gating stops.

guards.reason: asserts properties of the ROUTING AND ENFORCEMENT LOGIC, so its scope is the code it exercises plus the exemption switches it plants violations into -- not the whole tree. pdf_coupling.reason: only meaningful when a PDF changed

editorial.reason: the published prose surface. The exclusions are policy, not tidying: CLAUDE.md exempts tools/verify/** and tools/process/** from both prose gates (/rely covers those instead), and ZeroParadox/*.md are ride-along docs beside their .lean, reviewed as corpus rather than as publications. CLAUDE.md itself is excluded for the same reason it names -- operating machinery that asserts nothing about the mathematics, so editorial and adversary have no claim on it. .claude/commands/*.md is IN scope by CLAUDE.md R-EXEMPT: the gate briefs are published deliberately, as the artifact showing how this project reviews itself, so both prose gates fire on them; published-and-exempt is not a category to reason into. The blanket `.claude/*.md` exclusion was removed on 2026-08-25 because it silently cancelled that -- `*` DOES cross `/` here (measured: check_encoding's scope ["*"] covers 450 tracked files), so the blanket entry matched every brief under commands/. `*.html` was added 2026-08-29: the three interactive maps (bottom-family-tree, diagonal-family, snap-loop) are PUBLISHED and linked from README and GUIDE, and were in NO gate's scope until then -- `inventory` listed snap-loop.html under subjects_unscoped for adversary, editorial AND claim_review. The cost was measured, not argued: bottom-family-tree.html carried, twice, a citation R-BEDROCK prohibits in terms (`rInv_swaps` credited for a COINCIDENCE, when it proves an EXCHANGE between provably distinct points) while its .md sibling was corrected the same day, because nothing looked at it. `_layouts/*` is excluded because the Jekyll layout is chrome -- CSS and one routing comment, no mathematical content -- and it is excluded BY PATH rather than by narrowing the glob, so a new .html at the root falls INTO scope rather than silently out of it; same direction check_encoding's reason states for the same argument. ⚠ These are reviewed by AGENT and deliberately NOT by a glyph checker: the HTML entity-encodes every math symbol, so check_poles scores ZERO on these files and ELEVEN after decoding, and only 2 of those 11 were defects -- the other 9 are the ratified naming idiom, and the discriminator (swaps versus coincide) is semantic.

prior_art._registered_is_not_admitted: ⚠⚠ `actions: ["push"]` HERE DOES NOT GATE A PUSH, AND THAT SPLIT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS SAFE. This file is the REGISTRY -- what may be recorded and what a step is ABOUT. `admission.v1.json` is the ADMISSION SET -- what gitRobot requires green before it lets an action through, defaulting to NOT_ADMITTING. `prior_art` is registered for push and is deliberately ABSENT from admission, so it renders in the 'registered but not gating' line every run and blocks nothing at the ledger. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-09-01, twice, because the first fix was wrong: `coverage_gap` returns `steps: []` for a step that does not apply to the ACTION, and adding `scope` alone did NOT change that -- verified by calling it. A step must apply to the action before the ledger will emit a row for it, and the row is what `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` reads. So `actions` is required for the row to EXIST and `admission.v1.json` is what decides whether it BLOCKS; those were conflated in the revert of the corpus-wide promotion, which removed both and left the push leg unable to ask.
prior_art._scope_and_actions_are_different_jobs: `scope` says WHICH PATHS the step is about and keeps its records file-keyed. `actions` says WHICH ACTIONS it is evaluated for. The corpus-wide promotion of 2026-09-01 set both, was measured backwards (see `_reengaged` below), and was reverted by removing both -- which also removed the input `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` reads. Measured by /rely the same day: with no scope the leg gets `None` from `owing_paths`, correctly fails closed, and blocks EVERY push editing any `.lean` file, naming the wrong cause. Every layer behaved correctly and the composition did not. So: scope YES (the ledger must emit the row and keep the records file-keyed), actions NO (the ledger must not gate on a corpus-wide backlog). The per-file enforcement is the push leg, and it INTERSECTS this scope with the changed set, so the 215-file backlog `coverage_gap` reports is never demanded by anything.
prior_art._reengaged_2026_09_01: RE-ENGAGED under the first clause of `reason` below -- 're-engaged when .lean files are next touched' -- by Tim's decision. ⚠⚠ ENFORCED, BUT NOT FROM HERE, SO `actions: []` NO LONGER MEANS 'DISCIPLINE'. The obligation is now a BLOCKING push leg: `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` requires every `.lean` file a push EDITS to carry a passing `prior_art` verdict at its current bytes. Tim, 2026-09-01: 'whenever a specific file gets edited that that file is properly attributed. the current logic I think hits the entire corpus. and that is impossible to fill at one time.' ⚠ MEASURED WHY IT IS NOT A `scope` HERE: promoting this entry with `scope: ZeroParadox/*.lean` was tried the same day and is backwards on both counts -- it reports `have 3 / missing 215`, an impossible-looking backlog that does NOT block (narrowed coverage is reported, never enforced), while the only thing that DID block was an unrelated recorded FAIL, so a tooling push with no `.lean` in it was refused for a corpus finding. Per-file containment cannot be written as a static glob, and the push RANGE is knowable only in `batch.py` (REL-1). ⚠ THE ENDPOINT IS STILL verdictLedger R-8/R-9 (dynamic scope, then prior_art as a per-push obligation); when those land, that leg moves into the ledger and this entry gains a real scope. Until then the type stays registered so records remain valid and file-keyed, which is what the leg reads.
prior_art.reason: scoped to synthesis and bridge CLAIMS, not to files. Its trigger surface (ZeroParadox/*.lean, 218 files) is not its review surface, so no glob expresses what a run actually covers and a file-keyed record would overclaim. Narrowed 2026-08-23 by Tim's decision as ACKNOWLEDGED DEBT, not as a solved problem: re-engaged when .lean files are next touched, or as a dedicated batch. The gate is NOT retired and the type is NOT removed -- records remain valid and the type stays registered, so promoting it later costs one line.
prior_art._debt_not_closure_2026_08_23: TWO FENCES, because a narrowing is a weakening and this one must not travel. (1) It does NOT retire trigger 5: a new .lean file or >=50 inserted .lean lines still owes a prior-art search under CLAUDE.md. What changed is that the obligation stops being enforced by a per-push key it cannot express -- DISCIPLINE where it was briefly a gate, and this project's own record is that discipline leaks. (2) It is NOT precedent for rely / editorial / adversary, which are file-shaped, now scoped to 56/59/59, and stay blocking. The distinguishing test is CAN A GLOB EXPRESS WHAT THE REVIEWER READ -- yes for those three, no for this one. That is a property of the gate, not a shortage of effort.

rely._why: the /rely round signal. Read by batch.py, ship.py AND guards.py; `rely_cleared.txt` was its only representation, so retiring the signal path without this type deletes the coverage rather than migrating it.
rely._scope_warrant: ALL THREE PREFIXES batch.py's ROUTING sends to /rely, and this list is now MECHANICALLY ENFORCED equal to it -- guards.py, PROPERTY 'the registry scope and the router agree'. Do not hand-edit one side. History, because it is the argument for the check: `tools/process/*` was missing until 2026-09-01 while ROUTING carried it, guards asserted a warrant for it, and editorial and adversary excluded it via `tools/*.md` -- so a directory was exempt from both prose gates ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS STEP while this step's scope contained none of its files. An exemption is priced on the replacement gate actually being accountable; a scope that omits the files un-prices it silently. batch.py states the rule: 'That re-route is the entire warrant for the exemption.' ⚠ THE FIRST FIX OF THAT ADDED ONLY `tools/process/*` AND MISSED `.github/workflows/*`, THE THIRD ROUTED PREFIX -- in the same commit whose own note warned that a third prefix would inherit the identical hole. That is why this is a checker and no longer a sentence: the sentence was written and then broken by its own author, immediately.
rely.reason: governs the verification tooling AND the routed process prose. Its own brief FORBIDS running at full breadth -- rely.md step 1: 'SCOPE IT ... Do not run it at full' -- so with no scope the admission set demanded 477 paths from a gate that is not permitted to examine them. It was unsatisfiable by construction, not merely expensive.

claim_review._why: check_frozen demands it when a BASELINE ENTRY IS REMOVED -- the fail-closed record that an unexamined site had its liability discharged. With no type, deleting a baseline entry becomes free, which is a suppression mechanism losing its price.
claim_review._emitter_contract: MUST be recorded on EVERY run, not only when a baseline entry is removed: PASS when none was, and the discharge record when one was. A key that appears only sometimes is indistinguishable from a key nobody ran -- which is the enumerator-found-nothing defect, and the registry has no way to express 'conditional on an event' (its `when` is a PATH glob).
claim_review.reason: a removal is a removal FROM those baselines

agent_gate.reason: ADVISORY interpretation layer - it RECORDS but must never GATE. agent_gate.run() always returns 0 and batch.py deliberately does not increment `bad`, because the layer is fuzzy: measured 2026-08-21 before adoption, 1 false positive in 6 healthy runs, and byte-identical input returned TRUSTWORTHY twice and NOT_TRUSTWORTHY once. The >=2-of-3 vote takes that to 0 but the variance is real, and blocking on a coin flip is how a gate earns itself a bypass (CLAUDE.md rung 5: the screen may replace the enumeration, never the verdict). It is registered so that a CLEAN run leaves a record - verdictLedger.md section 2, 'a step that passes MUST emit a record; silence is never a pass' - which names this file as the measured instance of the defect. Its verdict is honest (it records what it found) and its status is non-gating, which is the registry/admission split working as designed.

check_fields.reason: ADVISORY reading list, registered so it can RECORD but gating nothing. Its JUDGEMENT half is computed from the Lean - it resolves each `field := binding` in every instance to a theorem or a def - and cannot be wrong. Its ENUMERATION half is a text scan over prose blocks and can be, so CLAUDE.md rung 5 applies: the screen may replace the enumeration, never the verdict. Registered 2026-08-26 after /rely RLY35-3: unregistered meant V8 refused every record, `--record` exited 2 for ever, and run_field_discipline turned that into a printed WARN while precommit still said PASS - a checker that runs, costs time, and can never leave a key, which is the exact 'silence is never a pass' defect one layer over.

check_claude_md.reason: the shape contract for CLAUDE.md itself, and it gates ONLY when that file is in the change -- Tim, 2026-08-26: a full re-analysis of it on every commit 'is nuts'. `when` is what makes that precise rather than a discipline: NOT_APPLICABLE on every commit that does not touch the file, REQUIRED and starting MISSING on one that does, so it fails CLOSED with nothing remembered. Registered after a measured miss -- unregistered meant V8 refused every append, the checker could never leave a key, and `inventory` never listed it, so R-NOTINLIB reached 36 lines against a 12-line cap as the largest entry in the file while '16 of 18 admission keys' read as near-complete. Same class as check_fields/RLY35-3, closed the same day. PUSH-TIME IS THE RIGHT MOMENT and that is a fact about readers, not a concession: the agent editing CLAUDE.md already holds the desired state in context, so the file's only real consumer is the NEXT session and a push is when it reaches one. NB a recorded PASS claims the two BLOCKING legs only -- rooted paths resolve, named checkers exist -- because the cap and history legs are WARN and three legs are declared PENDING and are NOT passing.

_switches_v15: A subject set is everything the verdict DEPENDS ON, not merely everything the checker read. Found by ZeroParadox 2026-08-23: check_pov recorded 291 subjects and NOT pov_baseline.txt, so grandfathering a violation into that baseline left the record reading SATISFIED -- every file it named was unchanged. V15 refuses a record that omits a declared switch, which turns a convention into a contract: with the switch as a subject, editing a baseline moves a blob the record names, the key goes STALE, and the checker re-runs. Declaring switches is NOT a narrowing and costs no reason -- it makes a type stricter.
_vendored_allowlist_2026_08_23: vendored_files.txt switched ELEVEN checkers off and was named by none of them. Found by ZeroParadox's /rely trial: a planted DENIAL made check_pov exit 1, one appended allowlist line made it exit 0, AND NO SUBJECT MOVED. Stronger than the baseline hole of REQ-10, because an allowlist removes files from SCOPE entirely rather than grandfathering sites -- the record does not merely go unstale, the thing it covered stops existing. The count reached eleven in two passes: seven whose records already named it, then four more that had not re-recorded because none is in the pre-commit hook -- the second time that cause has hidden a set.
